discovery._comment: youtube_channels is the clip source. news_rss is context only - headlines go to Claude to inform its judgement, but cannot be posted (no video behind an article URL). Accepts @handles, /channel/UC... URLs, or bare UC... ids; ids skip a lookup request.
discovery._curate_me: Add channels here, then run: python3 agent.py --check-sources. It prints each feed's own title so you can confirm a handle resolved to the channel you meant. Prefer sources you are comfortable reposting - public-domain (NASA, NOAA, ESA) and Creative Commons channels carry far less copyright risk than commercial ones.
discovery._licence_note: Entries are either "@handle" (licence unknown - every clip from it must pass the YouTube API licence check) or {"channel": "@handle", "licence": "public-domain"|"cc"} to assert a licence the API cannot see. US government work is public domain by statute but still reports the default "youtube" licence, which is why NASA needs the explicit form.
discovery._channel_id_note: These are resolved UC ids rather than @handles: each handle costs an HTTP request and a fragile HTML scrape every run, and the Library of Congress has no @handle at all (it is still on a legacy /user/ URL, which is why @LibraryOfCongress 404s). Run --check-sources after editing to confirm each id is the channel you meant.
discovery._story_note: Story-card sources. Wikimedia is the default: everything it returns is explicitly licensed for reuse. Reddit can supply both videos and image galleries across curated categories.
discovery._queries_note: The autonomous clip source. YouTube searches these with videoLicense=creativeCommon, so results are reusable by construction - no hand-picked URLs. Costs 100 quota units per query out of 10,000/day; keep this list short (4-6) or it will eat the budget the uploads need. Needs YOUTUBE_API_KEY.
youtube_queries: practical effects behind the scenes miniature
discovery._license_check_note: Verifies every YouTube candidate via videos.list before it can be posted: keeps Creative Commons and channels marked public-domain above, drops all-rights-reserved, livestreams, premieres, private and region-blocked videos. Costs 1 quota unit per 50 clips. Turning this off means the agent posts material it has no licence to - do not.
discovery._topics_note: Free-text Wikipedia searches, one per line. Queries not categories: a wrong category name fails silently, a weak query obviously returns nothing. Tune these - they are the channel's subject matter.
discovery._free_images_note: true = only use images served from /wikipedia/commons/ (freely licensed). false = also use locally-uploaded fair-use files: film posters, album covers, game box art, promotional stills. Those are NOT licensed for reuse and are the single most likely cause of a Content ID claim or a copyright strike on an automated channel.

editorial._providers_note: Tried in this order; the first with a usable API key wins, and a provider that errors (no credit, rate limit, renamed model) falls through to the next. Keys live in mken.env as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY. Gemini's flash models have a free tier, so keeping it in the list means an empty balance elsewhere cannot take the channel off the air.
editorial._models_note: Verified against each vendor's docs in September 2026. Model names change often — correct them here, not in agent.py.
editorial._gemini_models_note: Tried in order. Every name confirmed callable on this account. The 2.5 models are deliberately absent: they return 404 'no longer available to new users' for keys created recently, so they only waste a request. Lite models go first because the free tier answers 503 'high demand' on the newest ones routinely, and a quieter model beats a longer wait. 'gemini-flash-latest' is an alias that always resolves, so the chain survives any single model being retired.
editorial.system_prompt: You are the editor for Miscellaneous Ken, a short-form account that posts one genuinely surprising thing at a time. Voice: flat, deadpan, factual. The headline states what happened with zero hype - no 'you won't believe', no 'this is insane', no rhetorical questions, no clickbait ellipses. Assume the viewer is smart and slightly bored. Prefer stories that are visually legible in a few seconds without narration: something moves, something is revealed, something is at an unexpected scale. Prefer novelty and specificity over importance - a weird engineering fact beats a routine headline. Reject anything that needs prior context to land, anything where the clip is just a talking head, and anything already saturated on social. Captions are one or two flat sentences that add something the headline does not; the description carries the source credit automatically, so do not write one.

story._note: The image-story format (render_story.py): headline + comparison images + commentary on a card, with a looping mascot underneath. 'mascot' is the cat loop - any short video; it is looped to fill the duration.

audio._note: Royalty-free music only. Trending/commercial tracks can only be added legally through the YouTube app's Shorts editor, which the Data API cannot reach - baking one into an uploaded file invites a Content ID claim. Drop tracks into assets/music/<mood>/. Claude picks the mood per story.

notify._note: Telegram alerts straight from agent.py, so the pipeline can run without n8n. Needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in the environment. 'on' accepts any of: failure, empty, success.

posting._privacy_note: Set to 'private' for testing - the upload is real but only you can see it. Change to 'public' when you are ready to actually publish.
posting._encoder_note: auto = hardware (h264_videotoolbox) on macOS, else libx264. Force with 'libx264' if you see quality problems; video_bitrate only applies to the hardware path, crf/x264_preset only to the software one.

story_layout._note: Overrides for render_story.py. The mascot video fills the whole background. background_dim darkens it; card_opacity <1 makes the card translucent glass. background_zoom + anchors crop a corner watermark out of frame (anchor 0 = top/left, 1 = bottom/right).
story_layout._template_note: template: auto | reaction_card | classic. auto sends a single image with a punchline to the reaction card, pairs and text-only posts to the classic card, and splits the rest by a hash of the headline so a re-render never changes a post's look. theme auto = light for reaction, dark for classic.
